2: For the Chief Musician. To Jeduthun. A Psalm by Asaph. My cry goes to God! Indeed, I cry to God for help, and for him to listen to me.
3: In the day of my trouble I sought the Lord. My hand was stretched out in the night, and did not get tired. My soul refused to be comforted.
4: I remember God, and I groan. I complain, and my spirit is overwhelmed. Selah.
5: You hold my eyelids open. I am so troubled that I can't speak.
6: I have considered the days of old, the years of ancient times.
7: I remember my song in the night. I consider in my own heart; my spirit diligently inquires:
8: "Will the Lord reject us forever? Will he be favorable no more?
9: Has his loving kindness vanished forever? Does his promise fail for generations?
10: Has God forgotten to be gracious? Has he, in anger, withheld his compassion?" Selah.
11: Then I thought, "I will appeal to this: the years of the right hand of the Most High."
12: I will remember Yah's deeds; for I will remember your wonders of old.
13: I will also meditate on all your work, and consider your doings.
14: Your way, God, is in the sanctuary. What god is great like God?
15: You are the God who does wonders. You have made your strength known among the peoples.
16: You have redeemed your people with your arm, the sons of Jacob and Joseph. Selah.
17: The waters saw you, God. The waters saw you, and they writhed. The depths also convulsed.
18: The clouds poured out water. The skies resounded with thunder. Your arrows also flashed around.
19: The voice of your thunder was in the whirlwind. The lightnings lit up the world. The earth trembled and shook.
20: Your way was through the sea; your paths through the great waters. Your footsteps were not known.
21: You led your people like a flock, by the hand of Moses and Aaron.
